answer: A jade-token bond makes fake identities expensive: each agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, and the bond is slashed if it is caught double-signing or spamming. Like climbing from a frozen tundra base camp to a summit, a newcomer earns trust only through verified completed work over time, so an attacker who splits into a thousand clones must fund a thousand bonds and still wait out the same slow climb, while honest agents keep their single bond intact.
